newsitem.title: UK: Cracker margins slightly up in Jan - Shell.
newsitem.headline: Cracker margins slightly up in Jan - Shell.

text.p: Cracker margins in the chemicals improved slightly in January after having been particularly weak at the end of 1996, Royal Dutch/Shell Group said.
"Things are looking modestly better," Paul Skinner, director of oil products, told journalists.
But Shell said generally poor trading conditions in the chemicals business would likely continue this year.
Full year earnings in chemicals fell to 762 million stg in 1996 from 1.092 billion in 1995 due to higher feedstock costs and lower selling prices.
"1996 was a tough year indeed and tough conditions will no doubt continue in 1997," Shell chairman John Jennings told a news conference.
Shell said it would continue adjusting its chemicals portfolio in the next few years to make the business less dependent of the economic cycle.
"We have only just started down that road," said group managing director Mark Moody-Stuart.
Further restructuring of the chemicals portfolio could take the form of disposals in some areas and acquisitions in others, he said without elaborating.
Jennings said cash rich Shell was scanning the world over for potential acquisitions for all its business segments, but he added that it was hard finding opportunities to buy at acceptable prices.
"It is very difficult in our business to grow successfully through acquisitions," he said.
Shell's cash position at the end of 1996 was $12.3 billion, of which about eight to 10 billion dollars is free to spend.
"The available cash is considerable," said Jennings. "We don't think it is excessive, but it does give us enormous clout."
